summary: John Thompson Platts specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Balliol College until around 1881 and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford beginning in 1888.
John Vattanky worked in Indology and philosophy. He pursued his studies at the University of Oxford from around 1968 to 1971 and at the University of Vienna from around 1972 to 1974.

John Vincent Bellezza works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under Lopon Tenzin Namdak, Yungdrung Tenzin, and Tshering Choephel, and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

John W. Pettit specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Haverford College and under teachers including Ashok Gangadean, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Don Levi, later teaching at Oregon (1993–1994), College of Wooster (1994–1995), and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).

John W. Spellman worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Washington (around 1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (around 1967–2000).
John Wilson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1819 to 1828 and served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from around 1835 to 1842.

John Woodroffe worked in Indology and religious studies. After studying at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888), he served as a Judge at the Calcutta High Court (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).

Jokai Hiraoka worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), later holding posts at Shuchiin University and as a professor at Otemae University (~1980–1994).

Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT, and trained under Philip Kapleau, Jack Kornfield, and Joseph Goldstein. Working in religious studies and other fields, he founded and served as Professor of Medicine Emeritus at UMass Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal, holding posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, New York University, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, and held posts at Ryukoku, Kyoto, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later holding posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University, and Princeton University.

Jonathan Geen specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff and has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.
Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1963). He held a post at King's College London from around 1998 to 2013.

Jonathan Lear was a philosopher who studied at Yale University, the University of Cambridge, and The Rockefeller University. He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from around 1996 to 2025.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley, and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith worked in religious studies. He studied at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University, later holding posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1966–1968) and the University of Chicago (~1968–2016).

Jong-Nam Choi specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1990–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying under Ji-Gyeon Kim, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.
Jong-in Kim specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned a PhD at Stony Brook University by 2002, where he studied under committee member Sung Bae Park.
